input.summary:
Room 13 (upper hall and porch landing) is designed in parts/room-13.mjs: red runner, a hall table focal on the south wall, two settees, barrel plant stands, side tables, a card table with three chairs, and a chandelier. Furniture is drawn with layers() at y11..16.
A scratch build (build-check.mjs, build.check.nbt) writes the furniture past the lock: light is 8+ on every floor cell, and the interior render reads as a hall.
make.sh runs and writes build.nbt, but runParts refuses all 52 of this part's writes (the shell's air fills lock the room interiors), so the real build has 0 blocks from this part.
left: runParts locks every cell the shell filled with air (shell.mjs fill(...,'air') marks the room interiors as owned), so room parts can't place furniture in build.nbt: 52 REFUSED, 0 placed. Fix belongs in the shell or in runParts (air a part writes should not count as owned, or the room boxes should be left unfilled); not changed here, since it's outside this module.

Walk verdict is UNREACHABLE for the whole building, not just this room: even the entrance hall has 0 reached cells from the entrance, because joinery (front door) and colonnade are still stubs. Recheck `mcd room --only "upper hall and porch landing"` once those parts land; the stair joiner's landing (z53, y10) and stair top (z54) look right in the scratch build.
FIT reports 'hallway to nowhere' for the same reason (no entry yet), so it should clear with the joinery part.
plan.md is not ticked: this part is a room, not one of the six parts on the checklist, and it did not land in build.nbt.

waste.what: Cell-by-cell furniture layout: I drew the 18x6 floor grids by hand for six y-levels, then rewrote the sparse y12/y13 layers after getting the z indices wrong.
waste.cost: about 4 layer rewrites and one bad row-index fix; roughly 6 minutes of the 12
waste.tool: A sheet/cells helper in the build library (a list of [x, y, z, block, state] per room, rendered into layers() rows), plus a mcd plan variant that prints the grid with the y offsets in place.

waste.what: Working out whether a write was refused: I had to read runParts' lock logic in build.mjs to learn that air written by the shell is owned.
waste.cost: one grep and a read of the lock code, about 1 minute
waste.tool: make.sh should print the owner of each refused cell (for example 'owned by mansion shell: air'), and the room check should warn that the shell's air fills lock the room interior before any furniture is drawn.

waste.what: The scratch harness build-check.mjs copies the parts list from build.mjs by hand so I could place the furniture past the lock.
waste.cost: one new 25-line script and one run
waste.tool: runParts with report: null and an option to let a named part bypass the lock (or a --no-lock flag for room checks), so room designers can check their furniture without a copied build list.

Room 13 (upper hall and porch landing) is designed in parts/room-13.mjs: red runner, a hall table focal on the south wall, two settees, barrel plant stands, side tables, a card table with three chairs, and a chandelier. Furniture is drawn with layers() at y11..16.
A scratch build (build-check.mjs, build.check.nbt) writes the furniture past the lock: light is 8+ on every floor cell, and the interior render reads as a hall.
make.sh runs and writes build.nbt, but runParts refuses all 52 of this part's writes (the shell's air fills lock the room interiors), so the real build has 0 blocks from this part.
left: runParts locks every cell the shell filled with air (shell.mjs fill(...,'air') marks the room interiors as owned), so room parts can't place furniture in build.nbt: 52 REFUSED, 0 placed. Fix belongs in the shell or in runParts (air a part writes should not count as owned, or the room boxes should be left unfilled); not changed here, since it's outside this module.

Walk verdict is UNREACHABLE for the whole building, not just this room: even the entrance hall has 0 reached cells from the entrance, because joinery (front door) and colonnade are still stubs. Recheck `mcd room --only "upper hall and porch landing"` once those parts land; the stair joiner's landing (z53, y10) and stair top (z54) look right in the scratch build.
FIT reports 'hallway to nowhere' for the same reason (no entry yet), so it should clear with the joinery part.
plan.md is not ticked: this part is a room, not one of the six parts on the checklist, and it did not land in build.nbt.

waste.tool: A sheet/cells helper in the build library (a list of [x, y, z, block, state] per room, rendered into layers() rows), plus a mcd plan variant that prints the grid with the y offsets in place.

waste.what: Working out whether a write was refused: I had to read runParts' lock logic in build.mjs to learn that air written by the shell is owned.
waste.cost: one grep and a read of the lock code, about 1 minute
waste.tool: make.sh should print the owner of each refused cell (for example 'owned by mansion shell: air'), and the room check should warn that the shell's air fills lock the room interior before any furniture is drawn.

waste.what: The scratch harness build-check.mjs copies the parts list from build.mjs by hand so I could place the furniture past the lock.
waste.cost: one new 25-line script and one run
waste.tool: runParts with report: null and an option to let a named part bypass the lock (or a --no-lock flag for room checks), so room designers can check their furniture without a copied build list.
